phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Abstract interpretation analysis of EIP-1153 transient storage default value handling. ANALYSIS LIMITATION: This is a SPECIFICATION-ONLY check. Prysm is a Consensus Layer (CL) client written in Go, but EIP-1153 transient storage (TLOAD/TSTORE opcodes) is an Execution Layer (EL) feature that would be implemented in an EL client (like Geth, Reth, Nethermind, etc.). Therefore, no implementation code exists in the Prysm codebase to analyze. The analysis below examines the abstract state-space requirements from the EIP-1153 specification.

variables_identified.name: transient_storage
variables_identified.abstract_domain: Sparse nested mapping with potential uninitialized entries

variables_identified.name: address
variables_identified.abstract_domain: Set of all valid Ethereum addresses: [0x00...00, 0xFF...FF]

variables_identified.name: value
variables_identified.abstract_domain: Set of all 256-bit unsigned integers with distinguished default: {0, [1, 2^256 - 1]}
variables_identified.specification_requirement: EIP-1153 mandates zero return for unset keys

state_spaces.description: Collection of per-address transient storage tries
state_spaces.cardinality_bound: Bounded by number of unique addresses accessed in transaction

state_spaces.description: Per-address mapping of U256 keys to U256 values
state_spaces.cardinality_bound: Bounded by TSTORE operations within transaction (gas-limited)
state_spaces.initialization: Conceptually initialized with all keys mapping to U256(0)

abstract_transformations.precondition: address in Address domain, key in U256 domain

postcondition_cases.case: address in transient_storage._tries AND key NOT in transient_storage._tries[address]
address in transient_storage._tries AND key in transient_storage._tries[address]
postcondition_cases.state_anomaly_if_not: Incorrect value returned from existing storage

abstract_transformations.precondition: address in Address domain, key in U256 domain, value in U256 domain
side_effects: If address not in transient_storage._tries, create new trie for address
If value == U256(0), may remove key from trie (cleanup optimization)
If trie becomes empty after zero-write, may remove address from _tries (cleanup optimization)

potential_anomalies.title: Uninitialized Trie Pointer Dereference
potential_anomalies.expected_behavior: return U256(0) when trie does not exist
potential_anomalies.impact: Null pointer dereference, panic, or undefined behavior depending on implementation language
potential_anomalies.exploitation: Attacker calls TLOAD for never-before-accessed address, triggers crash or reads uninitialized memory
potential_anomalies.eip_1153_requirement: TLOAD MUST return 0 for any slot that has not been written to within the current transaction

potential_anomalies.title: Uninitialized Key Access Returns Non-Zero
potential_anomalies.buggy_transformation: return transient_storage._tries[address][key] without default value handling
potential_anomalies.impact: Smart contracts relying on zero-default for uninitialized transient storage will malfunction. Re-entrancy guards using EIP-1153 pattern (TLOAD == 0 as guard) will break.
potential_anomalies.exploitation: Contract expects TLOAD to return 0 for unwritten slot. If implementation returns garbage/non-zero, security invariants break. Example: re-entrancy guard checks 'require(TLOAD(slot) == 0)' at function entry and 'TSTORE(slot, 1)' to mark entered. If TLOAD returns non-zero for unwritten slot, legitimate first call is rejected.
potential_anomalies.eip_1153_requirement: TLOAD MUST return 0 for any slot that has not been written to within the current transaction

potential_anomalies.title: Cross-Transaction State Leakage
potential_anomalies.buggy_transformation: Fail to clear transient_storage._tries at transaction boundary
potential_anomalies.expected_behavior: transient_storage._tries = {} (empty) at start of each transaction
potential_anomalies.impact: Transient storage from transaction A leaks into transaction B, completely violating EIP-1153 semantics. All contracts using TSTORE/TLOAD will behave incorrectly.
potential_anomalies.exploitation: Transaction A sets TSTORE(addr, key, 123). Transaction B executes TLOAD(addr, key) and expects 0 but receives 123. Complete breakdown of transient storage isolation.
potential_anomalies.eip_1153_requirement: Transient storage MUST be cleared at the end of every transaction
potential_anomalies.note: This is related but distinct from CHK-0032 which explicitly checks transaction-scoping. Listed here for completeness of abstract state-space analysis.

potential_anomalies.title: Snapshot/Rollback Desynchronization
potential_anomalies.buggy_transformation: transient_storage snapshots not properly synchronized with persistent state snapshots during REVERT
potential_anomalies.expected_behavior: REVERT must restore transient storage to snapshot from begin_transaction, in sync with persistent state rollback
potential_anomalies.impact: After REVERT, transient storage is in wrong state relative to persistent storage, causing inconsistent contract execution
potential_anomalies.exploitation: Contract performs: TSTORE(slot, 1) -> nested call -> REVERT. If transient storage not rolled back, outer context sees TLOAD(slot) == 1 when it should be 0.
potential_anomalies.eip_1153_requirement: TLOAD and TSTORE follow the same behavior as SLOAD and SSTORE regarding call frames and reverts
potential_anomalies.abstract_domain_constraint: For all snapshot indices i: transient_storage._snapshots[i] must be consistent with state._snapshots[i]

potential_anomalies.title: Type Confusion in Default Value
potential_anomalies.abstract_state: Unset key maps to wrong zero representation
potential_anomalies.buggy_transformation: Return None, null, empty bytes, or wrong-sized zero instead of U256(0)
potential_anomalies.impact: Type mismatch causes EVM stack corruption or incorrect comparisons. Contract checking 'if (TLOAD(slot) == 0)' may fail due to type inequality.
potential_anomalies.exploitation: Implementation returns 0 as machine integer (e.g., int64(0)) instead of 256-bit zero. EVM expects 32-byte value on stack but receives different representation.
potential_anomalies.eip_1153_requirement: Default value MUST be U256(0), properly formatted as 32-byte big-endian zero
potential_anomalies.implementation_note: Language-specific: Go needs big.NewInt(0), Python needs U256(0), Rust needs U256::zero()

gas_limit_bounds.note: Gas limit provides natural upper bound on transient storage state-space size per transaction. Maximum possible state-space cardinality is O(gas_limit / 100) key-value pairs.

invariants_to_maintain.description: For any address without a transient trie, TLOAD must return zero

invariants_to_maintain.statement: ∀ address ∀ key: ((address ∈ transient_storage._tries) ∧ (key ∉ transient_storage._tries[address])) ⟹ (TLOAD(address, key) = U256(0))
invariants_to_maintain.description: For any key not present in an existing transient trie, TLOAD must return zero
Transient storage must be empty at the start of every transaction

invariants_to_maintain.statement: ∀ address ∀ key ∀ value: TSTORE(address, key, value); TLOAD(address, key) = value (within same transaction, no intervening TSTORE or REVERT)
invariants_to_maintain.description: TLOAD immediately after TSTORE returns the stored value (absent reverts)
REVERT must restore transient storage to the snapshot from the beginning of the reverted call context

key_requirements: Two new opcodes: TLOAD (0x5c) and TSTORE (0x5d)
Transient storage is transaction-scoped and cleared after each transaction
TLOAD costs 100 gas (warm access), TSTORE costs 100 gas
Transient storage behaves like SLOAD/SSTORE with respect to call frames and reverts
TLOAD returns 0 for any slot not written in the current transaction
Transient storage is not persisted to the state trie
specification_references.attacker_control: External attackers control transaction execution via TLOAD/TSTORE opcodes in smart contract bytecode

implementation_considerations.reason: Prysm is a Consensus Layer client. EIP-1153 is an Execution Layer feature. This analysis is SPECIFICATION-ONLY.

theoretical_implementation_patterns.code_pattern: if address not in transient_storage._tries: return U256(0); if key not in transient_storage._tries[address]: return U256(0); return transient_storage._tries[address][key]
theoretical_implementation_patterns.languages: Python, Go, Rust, all languages with hash maps

theoretical_implementation_patterns.code_pattern: Use language features for default values: Python dict.get(key, U256(0)), Go map with zero value, Rust HashMap with Default trait
theoretical_implementation_patterns.caution: Ensure default is exactly U256(0), not language-native zero types

test_cases_for_validation.description: TLOAD on address without transient trie returns U256(0)
TLOAD on address with trie but unset key returns U256(0)
steps: 2. Call TSTORE(addr, key1, value1) to create trie for addr
3. Call TLOAD(addr, key2) where key2 != key1

test_cases_for_validation.description: TLOAD after TSTORE returns stored value
TLOAD returns U256(0) format, not other zero types
steps: 3. Assert return value is exactly 32 zero bytes: 0x0000...0000
4. Assert return value type is U256, not int/null/None

test_cases_for_validation.description: TLOAD in nested call after REVERT returns pre-call value

boundary_analysis.boundary_description: EVM opcode execution to State Manager interface
boundary_analysis.attacker_position: External - controls transaction bytecode that invokes TLOAD/TSTORE
validation_required: Input validation: address must be valid 20-byte Address type
Input validation: key must be valid 32-byte U256 type
Default value handling: unset keys MUST return U256(0), not error/null/undefined
State isolation: transient storage MUST be cleared between transactions
Snapshot consistency: transient storage snapshots MUST synchronize with persistent state snapshots
consequences_of_failure: Re-entrancy guards using EIP-1153 pattern break (Critical severity for DeFi contracts)
Flash loan protection mechanisms using transient storage fail
Cross-function communication within transaction via transient storage becomes unreliable
Consensus divergence if different EL clients implement default value differently

formal_verification_goals.goal: Prove INV-TRANSIENT-001: Missing trie always returns zero
formal_verification_goals.approach: Symbolic execution with SMT solver: ∀ addr ∀ key: (addr ∉ tries) ⟹ (get_transient_storage(addr, key) = 0)
formal_verification_goals.tools: Z3, CVC5, or similar SMT solver

formal_verification_goals.goal: Prove INV-TRANSIENT-002: Missing key in existing trie returns zero
formal_verification_goals.approach: Symbolic execution: ∀ addr ∀ key: ((addr ∈ tries) ∧ (key ∉ tries[addr])) ⟹ (get_transient_storage(addr, key) = 0)
Bounded model checking over all possible TLOAD call sequences within gas limit
formal_verification_goals.tools: CBMC, KLEE, or fuzz testing with ASAN/MSAN

formal_verification_goals.approach: Model checking: Verify len(transient_storage._snapshots) == len(state._snapshots) at all times
